correctness.rationale: For an updated vertex with degree d and u equal-spin neighbors, the minority flip criterion is u>=ceil(d/2) and the change in monochromatic-edge energy is d-2u<=0. With k_j peripheral spins opposite to the hub, equal-spin counts are s-k_j and k_j-1. These give the exact odd/even closed classes; for even s local subset-inclusion graphs connect each hub sector and an all-balanced hub flip connects the sectors. Every outside configuration has a strictly energy-decreasing peripheral update, yielding the explicit stopped drift bound. Uniform measure on the even-s recurrent set follows from exactly symmetric reversible flips, and counting all-balanced states gives hub-colour conductance q^r/N and the mixing lower bound. A packaged checker exhaustively enumerates all terminal components for 21 (s,r) pairs through eleven vertices, independently verifying the formulas, exact ground-state energy and expected edge-flip energy changes; infinite correctness rests on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The original Stochastic Minority on Graphs text explicitly classifies a single complete graph (r=1) and supplies general energy descent, but does not state the recurrent census or bottleneck for gluing r>=2 complete graphs at one hub. The later accessible full text and section-level theorems were inspected. Further targeted searches of spin/minority literature and indexed mathematical records under windmill/friendship/block-graph/Ising formulations did not identify a stronger equivalent. Graph-invariant results on generalized windmills and previous classifications on wheels or tripartite graphs have different objects or update rules. Novelty remains bounded due to possible unindexed equivalences and unreadable older preprint body.

value.rationale: An unbounded natural two-parameter graph family of cliques with one shared hub tests whether zero-temperature local energy descent reaches global maximum cuts and how communication across a cut vertex depends on local parity. The result gives a full closed communicating-class census for every parameter, an exact irreversible/reversible parity switch, a uniform polynomial entrance bound, and an explicit exponential mixing obstruction despite unique recurrence. This is not a trivial restatement of the known single-clique case: the exponential boundary event requires all r blocks to balance simultaneously. It is mathematically meaningful even without a matching mixing upper bound.
